<a name="RevisionEvent"></a>
## type [RevisionEvent](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

RevisionEvent is one version of a record a store with [Revisions](#Revisions) keeps: its number — from 1, never given twice while the record exists —, when the write that made it ran, on the app's clock, zero for a record stored before its store kept revisions; who made it — the caller's [UserID](#UserID), empty for a write with no user —; which command made it — its node ID, empty outside a command —; and the record as it was, its secret members zeroed.

```go
type RevisionEvent[T any] struct {
	Number  uint64
	At      time.Time
	By      string
	Command string
	Value   T
}
```

<a name="Routine"></a>
## type [Routine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

Routine is a loop written by hand: a function that runs until its context ends. kit starts it with the app, cancels its context on shutdown and waits for it, restarts it after an error or a panic — backing off from one second to one minute — and reads its select statements to draw what it waits on.

```go
type Routine struct{}
```

<a name="ScopeValue"></a>
## type [ScopeValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

ScopeValue is one part of a path computed at the start: the user, the executable, a configuration directory. Two processes share a singleton or a socket when every scope gives them the same value.

```go
type ScopeValue struct{}
```

<a name="Secret"></a>
## type [Secret](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

Secret is a secret the product declares: provided by the operator — an SMTP URL, an API token — or generated by kit — a signing or sealing key — and rotated on its schedule.

```go
type Secret struct{}
```

<a name="Secret.Open"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Open](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Open(ctx context.Context, box []byte, aad []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Open decrypts a box any kept version sealed, with the aad it was sealed with. A box no kept version opens — forged, altered, or sealed by a version pruned since — is refused with an error errors.Is matches with secret.SealInvalid.

<a name="Secret.Present"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Present](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Present(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
```

Present reports whether the secret is set now, where it lives: false, and no error, when an [Optional](#Optional) secret is given nowhere — which the product answers by leaving off what needs it. An error says its store could not be read. A secret the start required is present, unless the operator took it back since.

```
if ok, err := OpenAIKey.Present(ctx); err != nil || !ok {
	return Verdict{}, err // no key, no automatic screening
}
```

<a name="Secret.Seal"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Seal](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Seal(ctx context.Context, plaintext []byte, aad []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Seal encrypts plaintext under the secret's current version, binding aad: data that travels beside the box in the clear and must come back unchanged for the box to open.

<a name="Secret.Sign"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Sign](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Sign(ctx context.Context, message []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Sign signs message with the secret's current version.

<a name="Secret.Value"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Value](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Value(ctx context.Context) (secret.Value, error)
```

Value returns the secret's current version. A provided secret is read where it lives at every call.

<a name="Secret.Verify"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [Verify](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Secret) Verify(ctx context.Context, message []byte, signature []byte) error
```

Verify reports whether a kept version signed message: nil when one did, and an error errors.Is matches with secret.SignatureInvalid when none did.

<a name="SecretConfigurer"></a>
## type [SecretConfigurer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

SecretConfigurer configures a secret.

```go
type SecretConfigurer interface {
	secretConfigure(o *secretOptions)
}
```

<a name="Service"></a>
## type [Service](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

Service is a bounded context of the product: it owns its building blocks — endpoints, stores, topics, subscriptions, workflows, jobs, frontends — and is the unit an App mounts. Declare one per package, as a package-level variable, and declare its building blocks through its methods:

```
var Service = kit.NewService("todos", "The todo list.")
var Todos = Service.Store("todos", func(t Todo) string { return t.ID })
var _ = Service.Endpoint("GET /todos", List)
```

Declaring never fails: a mistake — a malformed route, a duplicate name — is recorded with its source position and reported, all at once, when the App starts. The diagram shows it too.

```go
type Service struct{}
```

<a name="Service.Activity"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Activity](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/activity.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Activity(fn func(context.Context) bool) *ActivityHandler
```

Activity declares that the service is busy while fn returns true: a daemon whose clients are sessions, not connections, stops once the last session ended rather than once the last connection closed. fn is called on the idle watch's tick, from one goroutine, and must answer quickly; a panic counts as busy, and is logged. The value is kept for the declaration:

```
var _ = Service.Activity(func(context.Context) bool { return sessions.Open() > 0 })
```

<a name="Service.AuthHandler"></a>
### func \(Service\) [AuthHandler](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/auth.go>)

```go
func (*Service) AuthHandler[P, D any](name string, handler func(context.Context, P) (UID, D, error)) *AuthenticatorHandler[P, D]
```

AuthHandler declares the app's authentication handler. The handler returns the user's ID and data; an empty UID with a nil error means "no credentials", which [Auth](#Auth) endpoints answer 401 and [AuthOptional](#AuthOptional) endpoints serve anonymously; an error — usually [Unauthenticated](#Unauthenticated) — refuses the request.

The handler runs only for a request that carries at least one of the credentials' cookies or headers; a request with none is anonymous without asking it.

<a name="Service.CLI"></a>
### func \(Service\) [CLI](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/cli.go>)

```go
func (*Service) CLI(name string, doc string, fn CLIFunc, opts ...CommandLineConfigurer) *CLI
```

CLI declares a command named name, which Main runs when the process is called "\<binary> \<name> ...". doc is its one-line help.

<a name="Service.Command"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Command](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/command.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Command[C, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, C) (R, error), opts ...CommandConfigurer) *Command[C, R]
```

Command declares a command of the service: an operation named name, run by handler, that changes something. Its node is "\<service>/command/\<name>".

```
var PlaceOrder = Service.Command("place-order", placeOrder).
	Allow(Policy, "place", "order").
	Expose("POST /orders")
```

<a name="Service.Cron"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Cron](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/job.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Cron(name string, expr string, fn func(context.Context) error) *Job
```

Cron declares a job that runs on a five-field POSIX cron expression, in the process's local time zone.

<a name="Service.Endpoint"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Endpoint](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/endpoint.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Endpoint[Req, Resp any](route string, handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...EndpointConfigurer) *EndpointService[Req, Resp]
```

Endpoint declares an HTTP endpoint on route — "METHOD /path/{param}" — run by handler. The request is decoded from the path, the query, the headers (fields tagged \`path:"…"\`, \`query:"…"\`, \`header:"…"\`) and the JSON body (every other field), then checked against its \`validate\` tags, then handed to the policies ([RateLimit](#RateLimit), [Timeout](#Timeout), [Bulkhead](#Bulkhead)) and the handler. The response is JSON, or 204 No Content when it is [EmptyValue](#EmptyValue).

An endpoint is for what HTTP itself is about — a webhook a third party calls. A business operation is a command or a query, exposed on its route ([Command.Expose](#Command.Expose), [Query.Expose](#Query.Expose)), and run in process by the code that needs it ([Command.Dispatch](#Command.Dispatch), [Query.Ask](#Query.Ask)).

The endpoint's name, and so its node ID, is the handler's function name.

<a name="Service.Every"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Every](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/job.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Every(name string, period time.Duration, fn func(context.Context) error) *Job
```

Every declares a job that runs every period, first one period after the app starts.

<a name="Service.Go"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Go](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/loop.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Go(name string, run func(context.Context) error) *Routine
```

Go declares a hand-written loop. run must return when ctx ends; returning earlier, with or without an error, restarts it after a backoff.

Everything run does is drawn from the loop's node: a store it reads, a topic it publishes on. kit has no span around it — a run lasts as long as the app — so each of those calls starts a trace of its own.

<a name="Service.Implement"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Implement](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/endpoint.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Implement[Req, Resp any](port *PortService[Req, Resp], handler func(context.Context, Req) (Resp, error), opts ...EndpointConfigurer) *EndpointService[Req, Resp]
```

Implement declares that the service implements port: an endpoint of the service with no route, which only the port reaches, in process, when the app binds nothing else and this is the one implementation among the services it mounts. It runs as every endpoint does — the request's validate tags, the options' policies, the caller's user — and is named like one: its [Name](#Name), else its handler's name, else, for a function literal, the port's name. A handler whose request or response is not the port's does not compile. A host implements a module's port on its own service: it never adds a node to the module's.

```
var _ = posts.Service.Implement(desk.Enforcer, Enforce)
```

<a name="Service.Listen"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Listen](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/listener.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Listen(name string, contract string, handler ListenHandler, opts ...ListenerConfigurer) *Listener
```

Listen declares a listener named name speaking contract — "\<name>/v\<major>", "render/v1" — whose connections handler serves, one goroutine each.

<a name="Service.Loop"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Loop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/loop.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Loop(name string, run func(context.Context, WakeEvent) error, opts ...LoopConfigurer) *Loop
```

Loop declares a loop run by kit: run is called once at start, then on every wake.

Runs never overlap: wakes that come while the function runs are gathered into one run after it. A run that fails or panics is counted, and the next one waits a backoff — one second, doubling up to a minute — unless it is a [Loop.Nudge](#Loop.Nudge). A deadline already past wakes the loop at once, but never sooner than a second after the previous run: a WakeAt that keeps answering the past costs a run a second, not a spinning core.

<a name="Service.Mailer"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Mailer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/mailer.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Mailer(name string, opts ...MailerConfigurer) *Mailer
```

Mailer declares outbound mail.

<a name="Service.Name"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Name](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/service.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Name() string
```

Name returns the service name, which is also its node ID: qualified with its module's, "moderation.intake", when a module lists it.

<a name="Service.Port"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Port](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/port.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Port[Req, Resp any](name string, opts ...PortConfigurer[Req, Resp]) *PortService[Req, Resp]
```

Port declares a port of the service: an operation it needs, named name, taking Req and answering Resp, which another service implements ([Service.Implement](#Service.Implement)) or the app binds ([Bind](#Bind)). Its node is "\<service>/port/\<name>"; its doc is its declaration's doc comment.

<a name="Service.Query"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Query](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/query.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Query[Q, R any](name string, handler func(context.Context, Q) (R, error), opts ...QueryConfigurer) *Query[Q, R]
```

Query declares a query of the service: an operation named name, run by handler, that reads and changes nothing. Its node is "\<service>/query/\<name>".

```
var MyOrders = Service.Query("my-orders", myOrders, kit.Auth()).Expose("GET /orders", kit.AnyUser())
```

<a name="Service.Secret"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Secret](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/secret.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Secret(name string, opts ...SecretConfigurer) *Secret
```

Secret declares a secret the product needs.

Without an option it is provided: the operator gives it in the environment — the variable \<APP>\_\<NAME>, TODO\_STRIPE\_KEY for the secret "stripe-key" of the app "todo", or TODO\_STRIPE\_KEY\_FILE naming a file that holds it, the Docker and Kubernetes way — or in the environment's store, with \`kit secrets set\`. It is read at every use, so replacing it where it lives takes effect without a restart, and a start without it fails, naming the variable to set.

With [Optional](#Optional), a start without it goes on: the product asks [Secret.Present](#Secret.Present) before it uses the secret.

With [Generated](#Generated), kit makes it: version 1 on the first start, a new version on its schedule, the previous ones kept so that what they sealed or signed still opens and verifies. It lives in the store the environment keeps — an encrypted file store in dev, KIT\_SECRETS elsewhere. Its variable pins it: kit then uses the value as it is and does not rotate it.

name is 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit — one grammar for a file name and a variable — and unique in the app.

<a name="Service.Setting"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Setting](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/setting.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Setting[T SettingValue](name string, def T, opts ...SettingConfigurer) *SettingService[T]
```

Setting declares a setting of the service: name holds def unless the environment says otherwise — the variable \<APP>\_\<NAME>, TODO\_BASE\_URL for the setting "base-url" of the app "todo", or the key name in the product's configuration files. [SettingService.Get](#SettingService.Get) reads it.

name follows the secrets' grammar — 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit — and is unique in the app, among its settings and its secrets: the two share their variables.

<a name="Service.Static"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Static](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/static.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Static(name string, prefix string, fsys fs.FS, opts ...StaticConfigurer) *Frontend
```

Static declares a frontend serving fsys under prefix, which must end with '/'. A path with no file extension that matches no file serves index.html, so client-side routing works; a missing file with an extension — a script, a stylesheet — stays a 404. A directory is never listed. The SDK's static handler serves it; kit draws it and observes every request.

<a name="Service.Store"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Store](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Store[T any](name string, key func(T) string, opts ...StoreConfigurer) *StoreService[T]
```

Store declares a store of entities of type T, keyed by key.

<a name="Service.Subscribe"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Subscribe](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/topic.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Subscribe[T any](name string, topic *TopicService[T], handler func(context.Context, T) error, opts ...SubscriptionConfigurer) *SubscriptionWorker[T]
```

Subscribe declares a subscription of the service to topic. Delivery is at least once: handler must be idempotent, which is the one thing the SDK's queue cannot check and kit therefore asks you to promise here.

<a name="Service.Topic"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Topic](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/topic.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Topic[T any](name string) *TopicService[T]
```

Topic declares a topic carrying messages of type T.

<a name="Service.Watch"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Watch](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/watch.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Watch(name string, mark Mark, handler func(context.Context, WrittenEvent) error, opts ...SubscriptionConfigurer) *Watch
```

Watch declares a watch of the service: handler is told of every write kit confirms on a store whose entity holds a field that carries mark — the product's stores and the other modules', never those of the module the service belongs to (for a service of the product's, never the product's own) unless [OwnStores](#OwnStores) says so. The notice says which store, which record and whether it was deleted; the handler reads the record itself ([RecordsOf](#RecordsOf)). Delivery is at least once and in no set order, retried and dead-lettered after [MaxDeliveries](#MaxDeliveries) attempts: handler must be idempotent, and it hears the writes it makes itself on another's store — with OwnStores, never a write its own handler makes.

```
var Content = Service.Watch("content", kit.Moderated, Screen)
var Posts = Service.Watch("posts", kit.Moderated, Stamp, kit.OwnStores())
```

<a name="Service.Workflow"></a>
### func \(Service\) [Workflow](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*Service) Workflow[E any, S comparable](name string, store *StoreService[E], state func(*E) *S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

Workflow declares a state machine over the entities of store. state returns a pointer to the entity's state field.

func (*SettingService) Get() T

<a name="SettingService.Name"></a>
### func \(SettingService\) [Name](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/setting.go>)

```go
func (*SettingService) Name() string
```

<a name="StdioValue"></a>
## type [StdioValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

StdioValue is where a CLI command reads and writes: the process's own streams under Main, buffers in a test.

```go
type StdioValue struct {
	// In is the command's standard input.
	In          io.Reader
	// Out and Err are its standard output and error.
	Out         io.Writer
	// Out and Err are its standard output and error.
	Err         io.Writer
	// Interactive reports whether In is a terminal.
	Interactive bool
}
```

<a name="StoreConfigurer"></a>
## type [StoreConfigurer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

StoreConfigurer configures a store.

```go
type StoreConfigurer interface {
	storeConfigure(o *storeOptions)
}
```

<a name="StoreService"></a>
## type [StoreService](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

StoreService is a typed, keyed collection of entities. Every read returns a copy and every write stores one: an entity is kept as its JSON encoding, so what a handler holds can never alias what the store holds, and the memory and file backends behave identically.

With a data directory (KIT\_DATA\_DIR; ".kit/data" in dev) the store persists every write before returning, atomically — a crash never leaves a torn file — and a write costs one entity, whatever the store holds. Without one, it lives in memory. A store a database keeps ([Database](#Database), [Keeps](#Keeps)) lives in a table of it, and every call is a round trip. A store is a port (ADR 0004): what it runs on is its engine (store\_engine.go) — the SDK's document store, in memory, in files or over SQL —; kit makes it a node of the graph, observes every call, and speaks for its refusals. Its writes join the transaction their context carries ([Transact](#Transact)).

```go
type StoreService[T any] struct{}
```

<a name="StoreService.Count"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Count](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Count(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
```

Count returns how many entities the store holds.

<a name="StoreService.Delete"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Delete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Delete removes the entity with the given key, or returns a [NotFound](#NotFound) error.

<a name="StoreService.Diff"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Diff](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/revisions.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Diff(ctx context.Context, key string, from uint64, to uint64) ([]Edit, error)
```

Diff returns what changed from the version numbered from to the version numbered to of the record under key, in RFC 6902's words — add, remove, replace, each at a JSON pointer — with both values, in the order they apply: none when the two are the same. A secret member says it changed, never what. Showing a text's changes line by line is the reader's: the Studio does it.

<a name="StoreService.Erase"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Erase](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/privacy_erase.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Erase(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
```

Erase erases one record now, as its retention would: its personal, special and secret members and its subject cleared — after the store's Anonymise function has kept what it generalises —, its erased fields stamped, the rest kept. A held record is refused with a [Conflict](#Conflict) that names the hold, never a placed hold's reason. reason is journaled, for whoever runs the product.

<a name="StoreService.Filter"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Filter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/index.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Filter(ctx context.Context, keep func(T) bool) ([]T, error)
```

Filter returns the entities keep accepts, ordered by key. It reads every entity: an index is the way to avoid it.

<a name="StoreService.Find"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Find](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/index.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Find(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) ([]T, error)
```

Find returns the entities indexed under key, ordered by their store key. It reads any index, unique or not; no entity is an empty slice, not an error.

<a name="StoreService.Former"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Former](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/history_read.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Former(ctx context.Context, key string, pointer string) ([]Former, error)
```

Former returns the former values of the field at pointer — its JSON pointer (RFC 6901), "/email" — in the record under key, newest first: each with when it was replaced and by whom. A secret field's former values say when they changed, never what they were: their Value is empty. A field that keeps no former values is an [Invalid](#Invalid) error, a missing record a [NotFound](#NotFound).

<a name="StoreService.Get"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Get](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (T, error)
```

Get returns the entity with the given key, or a [NotFound](#NotFound) error.

<a name="StoreService.Hold"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Hold](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/hold.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Hold(ctx context.Context, key string, reason string) error
```

Hold places a legal hold on the record under key: neither the retention, nor a person's erasure, nor Delete touches it until [StoreService.Release](#StoreService.Release) lifts it. reason says why — an authority's request, a case under litigation — and is kept for whoever runs the product, never shown in the Studio. Holding a held record again replaces its reason.

<a name="StoreService.Insert"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Insert](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Insert(ctx context.Context, v T) error
```

Insert stores a new entity; it is a [Conflict](#Conflict) error when the key exists.

<a name="StoreService.List"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [List](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) List(ctx context.Context) ([]T, error)
```

List returns every entity, ordered by key.

<a name="StoreService.Lookup"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Lookup](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/index.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Lookup(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (T, error)
```

Lookup returns the entity whose key in the unique index is key, or a [NotFound](#NotFound) error. Asking a non-unique index is an [Invalid](#Invalid) error: use [StoreService.Find](#StoreService.Find).

<a name="StoreService.Passwords"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Passwords](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/passwords.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Passwords(field func(*T) *string, opts ...PasswordConfigurer) *PasswordPolicyService[T]
```

Passwords declares the password policy of one secret field of the store's entity; field names it — kit calls it on a zero entity to find which. The field then only ever holds the password's hash, a PHC string, or nothing before a first password; a write that puts anything else in it is refused. A field that is not secret refuses the start, as does a second policy on the same field.

<a name="StoreService.Put"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Put](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Put(ctx context.Context, v T) error
```

Put stores the entity, replacing any entity with the same key.

<a name="StoreService.Release"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Release](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/hold.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Release(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Release lifts the hold on the record under key: the retention takes it up again, from where its instants say. A record no hold keeps is a [NotFound](#NotFound) error.

<a name="StoreService.Restore"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Restore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/revisions.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Restore(ctx context.Context, key string, number uint64, fields ...string) (T, error)
```

Restore writes the version numbered number of the record under key back, as a new version: history is never rewritten. It restores the whole version, or only the fields named by JSON pointer (RFC 6901) — "/title" —, as WordPress restores some fields of a revision. It keeps the record's workflow state, which its workflow owns, and every secret member: restoring an account never brings back an old password past its policy, and naming one of them is an [Invalid](#Invalid) error. A unique index the restored record breaks refuses it with a [Conflict](#Conflict), and nothing changes. It returns the record as restored.

<a name="StoreService.Revision"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Revision](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/revisions.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Revision(ctx context.Context, key string, number uint64) (RevisionEvent[T], error)
```

Revision returns the version numbered number of the record under key, its secret members zeroed: a [NotFound](#NotFound) when the record keeps none of that number — never made, or pruned.

<a name="StoreService.Revisions"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Revisions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/revisions.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Revisions(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]RevisionEvent[T], error)
```

Revisions returns the versions the store keeps of the record under key, newest first: the record as it is now, then the former ones — n at most, more while a legal hold keeps the record. A secret member is zeroed in each: a former password hash never reaches the product. A missing record is a [NotFound](#NotFound), a store that keeps no revisions an [Invalid](#Invalid).

<a name="StoreService.Update"></a>
### func \(StoreService\) [Update](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/store.go>)

```go
func (*StoreService) Update(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(*T) error) (T, error)
```

Update applies fn to the entity with the given key and stores the result, atomically with respect to every other write of this store. fn must not change the key. An error from fn leaves the entity untouched.

fn runs while the store's writers wait — on a database, inside the write's transaction, the entity locked —: it may read this store, but must not write to it, nor fire a workflow over it — either would wait for the write fn is part of.

## type [TopicService](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

TopicService is an asynchronous channel of messages of type T. Every subscription receives every message, at least once: a subscription's handler must tolerate a redelivery.

```go
type TopicService[T any] struct{}
```

<a name="TopicService.Publish"></a>
### func \(TopicService\) [Publish](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/topic.go>)

```go
func (*TopicService) Publish(ctx context.Context, msg T) error
```

Publish sends msg to every subscription. It returns once every subscription's queue has accepted the message; delivery happens later. Inside a transaction ([Transact](#Transact), a command's) the message is encoded now and queued once the transaction commits: a rollback drops it.

<a name="WorkflowService"></a>
## type [WorkflowService](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

WorkflowService is a state machine over the entities of one store: the states an entity goes through, and the arrows between them. It is declared as data — which is why the diagram can draw it exactly — and it runs four kinds of transitions:

  - event transitions ([WorkflowService.On](#WorkflowService.On)), fired by code with [WorkflowService.Fire](#WorkflowService.Fire);
  - timer transitions ([WorkflowService.After](#WorkflowService.After)), fired by the workflow's own loop once an entity has spent a duration in a state;
  - timer transitions at an instant the entity carries ([WorkflowService.At](#WorkflowService.At)) — a due date, a deadline — fired by the same loop when it comes;
  - guard transitions ([WorkflowService.When](#WorkflowService.When)), fired by the same loop as soon as a condition on the entity holds.

The SDK's state-machine engine runs it (statemachine). Its loop never polls: it keeps an agenda of the transitions due, sleeps until the earliest, and a write of the store — which may bring one forward — wakes it. A workflow with nothing due does not run at all. Transitions of one entity run one at a time, of different entities at once.

The entity's state lives in the entity itself (the state function returns a pointer to it), so the store stays the single source of truth; the engine keeps, beside it, when each entity entered its state and the history of its transitions — in the workflow's file under the data directory, so a timer keeps counting across a restart.

```go
type WorkflowService[E any, S comparable] struct{}
```

<a name="WorkflowService.After"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [After](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) After[D Delay](event string, d D, from S, to S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

After declares a timer transition: an entity that has spent d in state from moves to state to, fired by the workflow's own loop. d is a duration, or a setting of the service that holds one — which must then be positive.

<a name="WorkflowService.At"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [At](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) At(event string, from S, to S, instant func(E) (time.Time, bool)) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

At declares a timer transition at an instant the entity carries — a due date, a deadline: an entity in state from moves to state to once the time instant returns has come; false means no instant for now. kit asks again each time the entity is written, and the workflow's own loop sleeps until the earliest instant.

<a name="WorkflowService.Can"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [Can](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) Can(e E, event string) bool
```

Can reports whether event may be fired on e.

<a name="WorkflowService.Census"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [Census](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) Census(ctx context.Context) (map[S]int, error)
```

Census counts the entities per state; every declared state is present. The engine keeps the count; the call is drawn, as the diagram declares it, as a read of the store.

<a name="WorkflowService.Fire"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [Fire](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) Fire(ctx context.Context, key string, event string) (E, error)
```

Fire moves the entity with the given key along the event transition leaving its current state. It is a [Conflict](#Conflict) error when no such transition exists, and a [NotFound](#NotFound) error when the entity does not.

<a name="WorkflowService.Initial"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [Initial](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) Initial(state S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

Initial sets the state a new entity enters with [WorkflowService.Start](#WorkflowService.Start).

<a name="WorkflowService.On"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [On](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) On(event string, from S, to S) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

On declares an event transition: [WorkflowService.Fire](#WorkflowService.Fire) with this event moves an entity in state from to state to. One event may leave several states, but only one arrow per (event, from).

<a name="WorkflowService.OnEnter"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [OnEnter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) OnEnter(state S, fn func(context.Context, *E) error) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

OnEnter runs fn when an entity enters state, before it is stored. An error cancels the transition, and so does a panic — reported as [CodeWorkflowHookPanic](#CodeWorkflowHookPanic), the entity free for the next transition. fn may change the entity, not its state nor its key ([CodeWorkflowHookChange](#CodeWorkflowHookChange)), and must not fire this workflow, which is refused ([CodeWorkflowReentrant](#CodeWorkflowReentrant)): transitions of one entity run one at a time.

<a name="WorkflowService.OnTransition"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [OnTransition](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) OnTransition(fn func(context.Context, ChangeEvent[E, S]) error) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

OnTransition runs fn after every transition has been stored, whoever fired it — the natural place to publish it on a topic. An error or a panic is logged and shown by the Studio; the transition stands, and the next hooks still run.

<a name="WorkflowService.Start"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [Start](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) Start(ctx context.Context, e E) (E, error)
```

Start enters a new entity into the workflow: it sets the initial state, runs the OnEnter hooks, and inserts the entity in the store.

<a name="WorkflowService.When"></a>
### func \(WorkflowService\) [When](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/workflow.go>)

```go
func (*WorkflowService) When(event string, from S, to S, guard func(E) bool) *WorkflowService[E, S]
```

When declares a guard transition: an entity in state from moves to state to as soon as guard holds. The guard sees the entity only: kit checks it each time the entity is written, never on a clock — a condition that depends on the time is an instant, declared with [WorkflowService.At](#WorkflowService.At).

<a name="WrittenEvent"></a>
## type [WrittenEvent](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/kit/decl_gen.go>)

WrittenEvent is what a watch is told of a write: which store, which record, and whether it was deleted — never a value. The watch reads the record itself ([RecordsOf](#RecordsOf)): without its secret members, and journaled.

```go
type WrittenEvent struct {
	// Store is the store's node ID: "shop/store/reviews".
	Store   string          `json:"store"`
	// Key is the record's key in the store.
	Key     string          `json:"key"`
	// Deleted is set when the write deleted the record: there is nothing
	// left to read.
	Deleted bool            `json:"deleted,omitempty"`
	// Fields are the store's fields that carry the watch's mark, as
	// [App.Fields] lists them. Which of them the write changed, the notice
	// does not say.
	Fields  []FieldRefValue `json:"fields,omitempty"`
}
```
